label: C-band grating coupler (input/output), 220 nm SOI
core_material: Si 220 nm on 2 um BOX (200 mm SOI)
process_name: 90 nm lithography SOI process, one-to-one 200 mm wafer run
notes: Pair of C-band GCs used as optical input/output of the CROW slow-light MZMs (Methods p.7); the loss value is stated with the 124 um modulator measurement (p.5). Authors call the coupling unoptimized; the paper also converts 5 dB to a 31.6 percent coupling efficiency (not entered separately). GC geometry not stated. label: Facet fiber coupling, etched x-cut LN rib

notes: Facet coupling loss stated once for the MZI and racetrack structures (p.3); coupler type (taper, lensed fiber) and fiber not stated. Numbers from arXiv v1 (2017-01-23), as for the EO rows. label: 2x2 MMI ring coupler (deep over-coupling), x-cut LN rib
core_material: x-cut LN 500 nm thin film (NANOLN), about 250 nm etch, 250 nm slab
notes: 2x2 MMI that over-couples the racetrack to the MZI arm of the RAMZI feng2022-a; loss and coupling measured on a standalone MMI on the same chip (Methods p.9), coupling said to agree with the design over 1500-1630 nm (no measured ratio given). Design: FDTD, core 31.4 x 4.8 um, input/output tapers 1.2 to 2.15 um over 15 um. The RAMZI budget attributes 2.2 dB to MMIs (number of MMIs not stated; not entered). LN film from NANOLN (supplier, a note). Fabrication by the authors at two institutions with thanks to individuals; no fab or facility org.

label: Reference racetrack (intrinsic Q), x-cut LN rib
core_material: x-cut LN 500 nm thin film (NANOLN), about 250 nm etch, 250 nm slab
notes: Reference racetrack on the same chip used to measure the intrinsic Q assigned to the RAMZI racetrack (Methods p.9); racetrack and waveguide designed top width 1.2 um. The authors give the corresponding intrinsic round-trip transmission tau 0.988 (no parameter). Reference geometry (length, gap) not stated; FSR 0.4 nm (50 GHz) of the RAMZI racetrack is in EO row feng2022-a. EO row holds the Q only in notes.

label: Cleaved-facet end-fire coupling with lensed fibers
core_material: x-cut LN 500 nm thin film (NANOLN), about 250 nm etch, 250 nm slab
notes: Devices cleaved for end-fire coupling (Methods p.9); lensed fibers at input and output, TE via polarization controller. EO row feng2022-a holds the coupling loss only in il_onchip_excludes text (8 dB for both facets).

label: NiSi ring heater with undercut, O-band Si MRM

All authors at GlobalFoundries; the paper does not state where the device was fabricated, so fab_org_ids is empty. EO rows hold the efficiency only in notes.

label: SiN microring with WS2 patch (ionic-liquid gating), 60 um radius
core_material: SiN 1.3 um x 330 nm waveguide, 30 um arc of monolayer MOCVD WS2 on the planarized ring
cladding: SiO2 100 nm (planarized), ionic liquid on top
notes: Ring used to measure the WS2 index change under ionic-liquid gating (Fig. 1); not an EO atlas row (the EO rows are the capacitor MZIs), so host_device_ids is empty. Fab org Columbia (D72 / D76) - the first author (Columbia EE) fabricated the composite photonic device (contributions p.13). Facilities - work done in part at the CUNY ASRC NanoFabrication Facility, the Cornell NanoScale Facility and the Columbia Nano Initiative shared labs (acknowledgments p.13).

label: Oxide-clad TFLT microring (power handling), before / after anneal
core_material: thin-film LiTaO3 on 4.7 um BOX on Si (NanoLN wafer), Ar+ etched rib; film thickness and etch depth not stated
notes: Passive microring of Fig. 1 (not the coupling modulator sayem2026b-cm). Annealed at 500 C for 2 h; Q rises by about 2x. Intracavity power up to about 4.2 W after anneal with maximum frequency shift about 1 GHz (about 160 MHz at 1 W; about 3.5 GHz at 1 W before anneal); no registry parameter for circulating power or power-induced shift (not entered). Fig. 1 also annotates Qe 851k (before) and 2023k (after), not entered (no external-Q parameter). Ring radius not stated. Annotated QL values are in the forward-scan panels, which the authors say can read artificially high before anneal. All authors at Nokia Bell Labs; co-authors fabricated the devices (contributions p.5). Wafer from NanoLN (supplier, a note). Polished facets, lensed fibers.
